dep_red_dog.name: Red Dog Mine
dep_red_dog.deposit_short_description: Red Dog, in Alaska's Northwest Arctic Borough, is the world's largest zinc mine and one of North America's most significant byproduct germanium sources. It is a clastic-dominated (CD/SEDEX) sediment-hosted massive sulphide deposit in which germanium substitutes within sphalerite; published work places Ge in Red Dog-type SHMS sphalerite in the 10-300 ppm range, with Teck not disclosing an exact deposit Ge grade. Teck reported 38.5 Mt of proven and probable reserves averaging 12.4% zinc as of the start of 2023 (an earlier 2018 figure was 57.6 Mt at 13.6% Zn). The mine produced 555,600 t of zinc-in-concentrate in 2024, with 2025 guidance of 430,000-470,000 t as grades decline. Critically, Red Dog recovers NO germanium on-site: the Ge-bearing sphalerite concentrate is shipped to Teck's Trail Operations in British Columbia, where germanium is recovered downstream. Teck is the largest germanium producer in North America (~8-10 t/yr Ge at Trail), but Red Dog's specific Ge contribution is not separately disclosed because Trail blends concentrates from multiple sources. Operated by Teck Resources under agreement with NANA Regional Corporation, which owns the land.

dep_middle_tennessee.name: Middle Tennessee Mines (Gordonsville / Elmwood / Cumberland)
dep_middle_tennessee.deposit_short_description: The Middle Tennessee Mines comprise the underground Gordonsville, Cumberland and Elmwood zinc mines plus a processing plant at Gordonsville, in Smith County, Tennessee. Mineralisation is classic Mississippi Valley-type (MVT): sphalerite in open-space fillings, breccias and fractures within Ordovician limestone and dolomite. The Middle Tennessee ore is germanium-bearing - it delivers recoverable germanium and gallium as byproducts to the Clarksville smelter - with concentrate germanium widely cited around ~400 ppm (the highest-grade Ge byproduct stream among the Tennessee operations; East Tennessee ore is not Ge-bearing). Nyrstar produced about 115,000 t zinc-in-concentrate across its East and Middle Tennessee mines in 2018. As of end-2025 the Middle Tennessee complex was non-operational and held under care and maintenance. In December 2025 Nyrstar (Trafigura) agreed to sell the Tennessee mines and the Clarksville smelter to Korea Zinc, a deal that closed in the first half of 2026; Korea Zinc plans to resume Gordonsville operations as part of its $6.6B 'Project Crucible.' Because dedicated Ge recovery at Clarksville is not yet built (construction from 2027, operations ~2029), the producing path currently yields NO refined germanium.

dep_pend_oreille.name: Pend Oreille Mine (Metaline)
dep_pend_oreille.location: Metaline Falls, Pend Oreille County, Washington, USA
dep_pend_oreille.deposit_short_description: The Pend Oreille Mine, about two miles north of Metaline Falls in northeast Washington, was an underground zinc-lead mine in the Metaline mining district. It first began lead-zinc production in 1952, operated intermittently, and was reopened by Teck Washington Inc. in 2004. The host is carbonate-hosted (MVT-style) sphalerite mineralisation; USGS sphalerite trace-element studies of the Metaline district include it among germanium-bearing sphalerite sources, alongside Red Dog and the Tennessee districts, though Pend Oreille's germanium was never commercially recovered. Teck permanently ceased operations on 31 July 2019, citing declining metal values, eliminating roughly 200 jobs. In April 2021 Teck transitioned the site from care and maintenance to formal closure, and remediation/cleanup of the historic debris field has since been overseen by the Washington State Department of Ecology. Because the mine is closed and never produced germanium as a product, this node TERMINATES with no germanium output.

dep_empire_state.name: Empire State Mine (Balmat)
dep_empire_state.location: Balmat, St. Lawrence County, New York, USA
dep_empire_state.deposit_short_description: The Empire State Mine (ESM) at Balmat, St. Lawrence County, New York, is Titan Mining's operating underground zinc mine in the Balmat-Edwards zinc district, hosted in metamorphosed Proterozoic carbonate (marble) with stratabound sphalerite. While ESM is a producing zinc operation, germanium is at the test-work / evaluation stage and is NOT yet produced. In October 2025 Titan announced it had found significant germanium concentrations within existing process streams: plant feed graded ~21 g/t Ge, enriching to 77 g/t in the pre-float stream (initial sampling on ~5,400 t of plant feed). In May 2026 Titan signed a cooperation agreement with Teck's Trail Operations to evaluate ESM process streams as germanium feedstock, targeting ~13,000 kg/yr (~13 t/yr) of contained germanium - drawn from scavenger tailings (~23 g/t over ~600,000 short t/yr) and pre-float tailings (~69 g/t over ~5,400 short t/yr). This remains explicitly evaluation-stage: the companies note recovery 'may not be economic on stated terms' and no binding offtake exists. Because no germanium is currently produced, this node TERMINATES. The ~13 t/yr is a potential future feedstock to Teck Trail, not realized output.

dep_apex.name: Apex Mine
dep_apex.location: Jarvis Peak, Tutsagubet Mining District, Beaver Dam Mountains, Washington County, Utah, USA
dep_apex.deposit_short_description: The Apex Mine in Washington County, southwestern Utah, holds the distinction of being the first mine in the world operated primarily for germanium and gallium. Originally a 19th-century copper-silver underground mine, it was recognised for exceptional germanium-gallium enrichment in oxidized/supergene zones (Ge and Ga grades reported 10-100x higher than typical deposits). Musto Explorations Ltd. brought it into primary Ge-Ga production in the mid-1980s; Hecla Mining Company reopened it in early 1990 with ~85 employees but ceased operations in August 1990 amid falling germanium and gallium prices. In its peak year the mine processed ~10,270 tons yielding ~5,634 lb Ge (~2.6 t), ~1,645 lb Ga and ~224,800 lb Cu. The mine has been closed since 1990; subsequent US germanium supply came from refining/recycling rather than Apex. In March 2026 Blue Moon Metals agreed to acquire Apex from Teck to advance US critical-mineral supply, but the mine remains non-producing. Because no germanium is currently produced, this node TERMINATES.

dep_brook_mine.name: Brook Mine
dep_brook_mine.deposit_short_description: The Brook Mine near Sheridan, Wyoming, is Ramaco Resources' coal-hosted critical-minerals project - Wyoming's first new coal mine in roughly 50 years, with coal mining commencing July 2025. Following ~18 months of core drilling and independent analysis by NETL/US national labs, Ramaco reports the coal and associated strata host rare earth elements (Nd, Pr, Dy, Tb) plus the critical minerals gallium, scandium and germanium. The July 2025 Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA) cites an exploration target of up to ~1.7 million tons of contained critical-mineral oxides within the permitted ~4,500-acre area, and projects ~1,242 short tons/yr of mixed oxide output (aggregating gallium, germanium, scandium, terbium, dysprosium, neodymium and praseodymium) at a planned 2 Mt/yr coal rate - germanium is not separately quantified at the annual level. Full mine-plus-processing-plant development is estimated at ~$533M; a $6.1M Wyoming grant supports a processing plant. The project is at the exploration/development (PEA) stage with no operating germanium recovery, so this node TERMINATES - no germanium is being produced.

smelter_teck_trail.name: Teck Trail Operations
smelter_teck_trail.deposit_short_description: Teck's Trail Operations in Trail, British Columbia, is one of the world's largest fully integrated zinc-lead smelting and refining complexes and the ONLY commercial-scale primary germanium recovery facility in North America. Germanium is recovered as a byproduct of zinc concentrate processing: residues from zinc concentrates are treated in roasters or pressure-leach circuits and purified to produce germanium dioxide and other byproduct metals. Most of Trail's germanium feed comes from Red Dog-district (Alaska) sphalerite concentrate, supplemented by other zinc concentrates. Trail currently recovers approximately 8-10 tonnes per year of germanium, making Teck North America's largest germanium producer and the fourth largest globally; the company has signaled a planned ~4 t/yr expansion by 2027 and is evaluating additional feedstock (e.g., ~13,000 kg/yr potential from Titan Mining's Empire State Mine waste streams). In Q1 2026, higher byproduct prices (notably silver and germanium) boosted Trail's results while volumes held roughly flat year-on-year. Trail is the node where Red Dog's contained germanium is actually converted into a marketable raw material, feeding the germanium raw-material class boundary.

smelter_nyrstar_clarksville.name: Nyrstar Clarksville (Korea Zinc) Smelter
smelter_nyrstar_clarksville.deposit_short_description: The Clarksville smelter in Montgomery County, Tennessee, is the sole primary zinc smelter in the United States. It historically processed germanium- and gallium-bearing zinc concentrate from the Middle Tennessee Mines, depositing Ge/Ga-rich residues in on-site ponds, but it has NEVER operated a commercial germanium recovery circuit. Nyrstar (Trafigura) proposed a dedicated germanium-gallium recovery and processing facility - initially a ~$90M project, later cited at ~$150M - targeting up to ~30 t/yr germanium and ~40 t/yr gallium (claimed potential ~80% of US Ge/Ga demand), but the facility was never built. In December 2025 Nyrstar agreed to sell Clarksville and the Tennessee mines to Korea Zinc, closing in H1 2026. Korea Zinc launched its $6.6B (total $7.4B) 'Project Crucible' in April 2026; site preparation and engineering run through 2026, construction begins early 2027 (~33-month build), with initial zinc operations targeted for 2029 and critical-mineral (Ge/Ga/In) recovery from ~620,000 t of stored residues thereafter. Because dedicated germanium recovery is NOT yet operational, Clarksville currently produces NO refined germanium - the Middle Tennessee germanium path TERMINATES here until the recovery plant comes online (~2029).

co_teck.name: Teck Resources Limited
co_teck.description: Diversified Canadian miner and operator of the Red Dog zinc mine (Alaska) and Trail Operations (BC). Teck is North America's largest germanium producer and ~4th largest globally, recovering approximately 8-10 t/yr of germanium at Trail as a byproduct of zinc concentrate refining (principally Red Dog-district feed), with a ~4 t/yr expansion planned by 2027. Red Dog produced 555,600 t zinc-in-concentrate in 2024 (2025 guidance 430,000-470,000 t). Teck also formerly owned the closed Pend Oreille mine (WA, ceased 2019) and the historic Apex Ge-Ga mine (UT), which it agreed to sell to Blue Moon Metals in 2026.

co_korea_zinc.name: Korea Zinc Inc. (formerly Nyrstar / Trafigura)
co_korea_zinc.description: Korea Zinc acquired Nyrstar's US operations - the Middle Tennessee Mines and the Clarksville smelter (the only primary zinc smelter in the US) - from Trafigura, with the deal closing in H1 2026. Nyrstar had proposed (~$90-150M) a dedicated germanium-gallium recovery plant at Clarksville targeting ~30 t/yr Ge and ~40 t/yr Ga, but it was never built; the Middle Tennessee ore carries ~400 ppm Ge in concentrate. Korea Zinc's $6.6B 'Project Crucible' (total $7.4B) will rebuild and expand Clarksville to recover Ge/Ga/In from ~620,000 t of stored residues - construction from early 2027, initial operations ~2029. No refined germanium is produced today.

co_blue_moon.description: Junior explorer that agreed in March 2026 to acquire the historic Apex germanium-gallium mine (Washington County, Utah) from Teck Resources to advance US critical-mineral supply.
